ep.eq.intro.text: This is the Comet Cat. It filled two bags with star sand, the same amount in each, and it has a puzzle for you: how heavy is one bag?
ep.eq.intro.heard: This is the Comet Cat. It filled two bags with star sand, the same amount in each, and it has a puzzle for you. How heavy is one bag?

ep.eq.scale.text: The two bags and 3 loose weights go on one side of a balance. Every weight is the same. Watch the other side as weights go on, one at a time.
ep.eq.scale.heard: The two bags and three loose weights go on one side of a balance. Every weight is the same. Watch the other side as weights go on, one at a time.

ep.eq.level.text: With 11 weights it hangs level. Level means both sides weigh the same, so the two bags and the 3 loose weights together weigh as much as 11 weights.
ep.eq.level.heard: With 11 weights it hangs level. Level means both sides weigh the same, so the two bags and the three loose weights together weigh as much as 11 weights.

ep.eq.letter.text: The Comet Cat wrote x on each bag. x stands for how many weights one bag weighs: a number we don't know yet. Both bags say x because they weigh the same.
ep.eq.letter.heard: The comet cat wrote X on each bag. X stands for how many weights one bag weighs, a number we don't know yet. Both bags say X because they weigh the same.

ep.eq.guess.text: How many weights do you think one bag weighs? Make a guess. Any guess can be tested on the balance.
ep.eq.guess.heard: How many weights do you think one bag weighs? Make a guess. Any guess can be tested on the balance.

ep.eq.try.you.text: Let's test {n}. If one bag really weighs that much, the balance will still hang level when that many weights go in each bag's place.
ep.eq.try.you.heard: Let's test your number. If one bag really weighs that much, the balance will still hang level when that many weights go in each bag's place.

ep.eq.try.again.text: Let's test {n} in each bag's place.
ep.eq.try.again.heard: Let's test your number in each bag's place.

ep.eq.heavy.text: With {n} in place of each bag, the bags' side comes to {m} weights. That's more than the {k} on the other side, and the heavier side goes down. So one bag weighs less than {n}.
ep.eq.heavy.heard: With your number in place of each bag, the bag's side comes to more weights than the other side has, and the heavier side goes down. So one bag weighs less than your number.

ep.eq.light.text: With {n} in place of each bag, the bags' side comes to {m} weights. That's less than the {k} on the other side, and the lighter side goes up. So one bag weighs more than {n}.
ep.eq.light.heard: With your number in place of each bag, the bag's side comes to fewer weights than the other side has, and the lighter side goes up. So one bag weighs more than your number.

ep.eq.lucky.text: With 4 in each bag's place, it stayed level: 4 and 4 and 3 make 11, so you found it. Now let's find it without guessing, for numbers that are hard to guess.
ep.eq.lucky.heard: With four in each bag's place, it stayed level. Four and four and three make eleven, so you found it. Now let's find it without guessing, for numbers that are hard to guess.

ep.eq.unlucky.text: Guessing can take a lot of tries, so let's work it out instead, one step at a time, by taking things off the balance.
ep.eq.unlucky.heard: Guessing can take a lot of tries, so let's work it out instead, one step at a time, by taking things off the balance.

ep.eq.own.why.text: If one bag sat on its side alone and the balance hung level, we could count the weights on the other side to see how heavy the bag is. So we want a bag on its own.
ep.eq.own.why.heard: If one bag sat on its side alone and the balance hung level, we could count the weights on the other side to see how heavy the bag is. So we want a bag on its own.

ep.eq.try.off.text: First the 3 loose weights come off the bags' side only. Drag them off, and watch what the balance does.
ep.eq.try.off.heard: First, the three loose weights come off the bag's side only. Drag them off, and watch what the balance does.

ep.eq.off.up.text: The bags' side went up. You took 3 weights off it and nothing off the other side, so the bags' side is lighter now, and the lighter side goes up.
ep.eq.off.up.heard: The bag's side went up. You took three weights off it and nothing off the other side, so the bag's side is lighter now, and the lighter side goes up.

ep.eq.other.ask.text: The two sides weighed the same before. How many weights must come off the other side to make it level again?
ep.eq.other.ask.heard: The two sides weighed the same before. How many weights must come off the other side to make it level again?

ep.eq.try.other.text: Let's take your {n} off the other side.
ep.eq.try.other.heard: Let's take your number off the other side.

ep.eq.other.yes.text: Level again. Both sides lost 3 weights, so they still weigh the same. 11 take away 3 is 8, so the two bags together weigh as much as 8 weights.
ep.eq.other.yes.heard: Level again. Both sides lost three weights, so they still weigh the same. Eleven take away three is eight, so the two bags together weigh as much as eight weights.

ep.eq.other.few.text: Your {n} wasn't enough: the other side is still heavier, so it stays down. The bags' side lost 3, so the other side has to lose 3 too.
ep.eq.other.few.heard: Your number wasn't enough. The other side is still heavier, so it stays down. The bag side lost three, so the other side has to lose three too.

ep.eq.other.many.text: Your {n} was too many: now the other side is lighter, so it went up. The bags' side lost 3, so the other side has to lose 3 too.
ep.eq.other.many.heard: Your number was too many. Now the other side is lighter, so it went up. The bag side lost three, so the other side has to lose three too.

ep.eq.other.fix.text: With 3 off the other side, it's level again, because both sides lost the same. 11 take away 3 is 8, so the two bags together weigh as much as 8 weights.
ep.eq.other.fix.heard: With three off the other side, it's level again because both sides lost the same. Eleven take away three is eight, so the two bags together weigh as much as eight weights.

ep.eq.share.ask.text: How many weights must come off the other side with the bag, so the balance stays level?
ep.eq.share.ask.heard: How many weights must come off the other side with the bag so the balance stays level?

ep.eq.try.share.heard: Let's take one bag off and your number off the other side.

ep.eq.share.yes.heard: It stayed level with 4. One bag is half of the bag's side, and half of the 8 weights is 4. So X is 4.

ep.eq.share.few.heard: Your number wasn't enough. The other side went down, so the weights still on it are heavier than the one bag that's left.

ep.eq.share.many.heard: Your number was too many. The other side went up, so the weights still on it are lighter than the one bag that's left.

ep.eq.share.how.text: Let's put them back. Here's a way to be sure: the two bags weigh the same, so the 8 weights are shared into 2 equal piles, one for each bag.
ep.eq.share.how.heard: Let's put them back. Here's a way to be sure. The two bags weigh the same, so the eight weights are shared into two equal piles, one for each bag.

ep.eq.write.heard: Here is what we did written down. The first line is the balance at the start. 2x means the two bags that each weigh x, the 3 is the loose weights, and 11 is the other side.

ep.eq.write.read.text: The = sign means the two sides weigh the same. Taking 3 off both sides gave 2x = 8. Then keeping half of each side gave x = 4.

ep.check.text: Quick check! Do you still remember this trick?

ep.count-on.intro.text: Welcome to the dock! Puddle Pup loves hopping along the planks, and every plank has a number. Let's use the hops to add.
ep.count-on.intro.heard: Welcome to the dock. Puddle Pup loves hopping along the planks, and every plank has a number. Let's use the hops to add.

ep.count-on.s0.heard: 6 plus 2. Start at the bigger number, 6.

ep.count-on.s1.text: Now count on. Hop 1 plank, to 7.
ep.count-on.s1.heard: Now count on, hop one plank to seven.

ep.count-on.s2.heard: Hop one more to 8, so 6 plus 2 makes 8.

ep.count-on.s3.text: Plus 1 is just the next number. Plus 0 changes nothing at all!
ep.count-on.s3.heard: Plus 1 is just the next number. Plus 0 changes nothing at all.

ep.count-on.card.text: You won the Count On card! Start at the big number and hop on.

ep.doubles.intro.text: Sprout Bunny is baking cookies, and Bunny always bakes them in pairs. Let's find the doubles!
ep.doubles.intro.heard: Sprout Bunny is baking cookies, and Bunny always bakes them in pairs. Let's find the doubles.

ep.doubles.s0.text: Doubles are two of the same. Here are 6 cookies.
ep.doubles.s0.heard: Doubles are two of the same. Here are six cookies.

ep.doubles.s1.text: And 6 more, just like a mirror! 6 + 6 = 12.
ep.doubles.s1.heard: and 6 more, just like a mirror. 6 plus 6 makes 12.

ep.doubles.s2.text: 6 + 7 is a near double. It's the double, and 1 more.
ep.doubles.s2.heard: 6 plus 7 is a near double. It's the double, and one more.

ep.doubles.card.text: You won the Doubles card! Two of the same, and one more for a near double.
ep.doubles.card.heard: You won the doubles card. Two of the same, and one more for a near double.

ep.bridge-ten.intro.text: Sprout Bunny baked 8 cookies, and then 5 more. Instead of counting them all, let's fill a ten first!
ep.bridge-ten.intro.heard: Sprout Bunny baked 8 cookies, and then 5 more. Instead of counting them all, let's fill a 10 first.

ep.bridge-ten.s0.text: 8 + 5. That's 8 cookies in one tin, and 5 in the other.
ep.bridge-ten.s0.heard: Eight plus five. That's eight cookies in one tin and five in the other.

ep.bridge-ten.s1.text: Move 2 over to fill the ten!

ep.bridge-ten.s2.text: A full ten and 3 more make 13!

ep.bridge-ten.card.text: You won the Make Ten First card! Fill the ten, then add the rest.
ep.bridge-ten.card.heard: You won the make 10 first card. Fill the 10, then add the rest.

ep.count-back.intro.text: Back at the dock! This time Puddle Pup hops backwards, to take away.
ep.count-back.intro.heard: Back at the dock. This time Puddle Pup hops backwards to take away.

ep.count-back.s1.text: Now count back. Hop 1 plank, to 8.
ep.count-back.s1.heard: Now count back, hop one plank, to eight.

ep.count-back.s2.heard: Hop one more to seven. So nine take away two is seven.

ep.count-back.s3.text: Take away 1 is the number just before. Take away 0, and nothing changes!
ep.count-back.s3.heard: Takeaway 1 is the number just before. Takeaway 0 and nothing changes.

ep.count-back.card.text: You won the Count Back card! Start at the big number and hop back.
ep.count-back.card.heard: You won the Count Back Card. Start at the big number and hop back.

ep.doubles-back.intro.text: Snowdrop Seal packed the picnic berries in pairs. A double can help us take away, too!
ep.doubles-back.intro.heard: Snowdrop Seal packed the picnic berries in pairs. A double can help us take away two.

ep.doubles-back.s1.text: Take one row away, and 7 are left. 14 − 7 = 7!
ep.doubles-back.s1.heard: Take one row away, and seven are left. Fourteen take away, seven is seven.

ep.doubles-back.s2.text: What about taking away 10? 16 is a full ten and 6 more.
ep.doubles-back.s2.heard: What about taking away 10? 16 is a full 10 and 6 more.

ep.doubles-back.s3.text: The ten goes, and the 6 stay. 16 − 10 = 6!
ep.doubles-back.s3.heard: The 10 goes, and the 6 stay. 16 take away 10 is 6.

ep.doubles-back.card.text: You won the Doubles Back card! Use a double backwards.
ep.doubles-back.card.heard: You won the doubles back card. Use a double backwards.

ep.dec-coins.intro.text: Welcome to the Sky Market! Rock Candy Armadillo rolled in with a pile of coins. Let's count them, biggest first.
ep.dec-coins.intro.heard: Welcome to the Sky Market. Rock Candy Armadillo rolled in with a pile of coins. Let's count them, biggest first.

ep.dec-coins.s0.text: Here are four coins. A penny, a nickel, a dime and a quarter. Each one is worth a different amount.
ep.dec-coins.s0.heard: Here are four coins. A penny, a nickel, a dime, and a quarter. Each one is worth a different amount.

ep.dec-coins.s1.text: Tap each coin to see what it's worth. A penny is 1 cent, a nickel is 5, a dime is 10, and a quarter is 25.
ep.dec-coins.s1.heard: Tap each coin to see what it's worth. A penny is one cent, a nickel is five, a dime is ten, and a quarter is twenty-five.

ep.dec-coins.s2.text: Rock Candy Armadillo's pile has five coins, all mixed up. To count them, line them up biggest first.
ep.dec-coins.s2.heard: Rock Candy Armadillo's pile has five coins, all mixed up. To count them, line them up biggest first.

ep.dec-coins.s3.text: Drag the coins into a line, from the biggest to the smallest.
ep.dec-coins.s3.heard: Drag the coins into a line, from the biggest to the smallest.

ep.dec-coins.s4.text: Now tap each coin and count on. 25, 35, 45, then 50, and 51 cents!
ep.dec-coins.s4.heard: Now tap each coin and count on. 25, 35, 45, then 50 and 51 cents.

ep.dec-coins.card.text: You won the Biggest First card! Line the coins up from biggest to smallest, then count on.
ep.dec-coins.card.heard: You won the biggest first card. Line the coins up from biggest to smallest, then count on.

ep.dec-change.intro.text: Teakettle Dragon runs the lemonade stall. A lemonade costs 35 cents, and the shopper pays 50 cents. How much change?
ep.dec-change.intro.heard: Teakettle Dragon runs the Lemonade Stall. A lemonade costs 35 cents, and the shopper pays 50 cents. How much change?

ep.dec-change.s0.text: The lemonade costs 35 cents. The shopper pays with two quarters. That's 50 cents.
ep.dec-change.s0.heard: The lemonade costs 35 cents. The shopper pays with two quarters. That's 50 cents.

ep.dec-change.s1.text: Shopkeepers count up from the price. Tap the glowing spot to start at 35.
ep.dec-change.s1.heard: Shopkeepers count up from the price. Tap the glowing spot to start at $35.

ep.dec-change.s2.text: Drag a nickel onto the plate. That makes 40. Then a dime. That makes 50!
ep.dec-change.s2.heard: Drag a nickel onto the plate. That makes 40. Then a dime. That makes 50.

ep.dec-change.s3.text: The change is the coins you counted, a nickel and a dime. That's 15 cents!
ep.dec-change.s3.heard: The change is the coins you counted. A nickel and a dime. That's 15 cents.

ep.dec-change.card.text: You won the Count Up card! Start at the price, and count up to what they paid.
ep.dec-change.card.heard: You won the count-up card. Start at the price and count up to what they paid.

ep.dec-tenths.intro.text: Popcorn Puffling found a chocolate bar with 10 pieces. Each piece is one tenth!
ep.dec-tenths.intro.heard: Popcorn Puffling found a chocolate bar with 10 pieces. Each piece is 1 tenth.

ep.dec-tenths.s0.text: The whole bar is 1. It snaps into 10 equal pieces.
ep.dec-tenths.s0.heard: The whole bar is one. It snaps into 10 equal pieces.

ep.dec-tenths.s1.text: Snap off one piece, and put it on the plate. One piece is one tenth. We write it 0.1.
ep.dec-tenths.s1.heard: Snap off one piece and put it on the plate. One piece is one-tenth. We write it 0.1.

ep.dec-tenths.s2.text: Snap off two more. Three pieces are three tenths. That's 0.3.
ep.dec-tenths.s2.heard: Snap off two more. Three pieces are three tenths. That's 0.3.

ep.dec-tenths.s3.text: The first digit after the point counts tenths. Tap each glowing spot. 3 pieces make 0.3, and the 7 left make 0.7.
ep.dec-tenths.s3.heard: The first number after the point counts tenths. Tap each glowing spot. Three pieces make 0.3, and the seven left make 0.7.

ep.dec-tenths.card.text: You won the Tenths card! The first digit after the point counts tenths.
ep.dec-tenths.card.heard: You won the tenths card. The first number after the point counts tenths.

ep.dec-hundredths.intro.text: Geode Mole dug up a giant chocolate slab of 100 squares. Each square is one hundredth.
ep.dec-hundredths.intro.heard: Geode Mole dug up a giant chocolate slab of a hundred squares. Each square is one hundredth.

ep.dec-hundredths.s0.heard: A hundred squares make one whole slab.

ep.dec-hundredths.s1.text: Tap the glowing square. One square is one hundredth. We write it 0.01.
ep.dec-hundredths.s1.heard: Tap the glowing square. One square is one hundredth. We write it 0.01.

ep.dec-hundredths.s2.text: Tap the glowing row. A row of 10 squares is one tenth. That's 0.1, the same as 0.10.
ep.dec-hundredths.s2.heard: Tap the glowing row. A row of 10 squares is 1 tenth. That's 0.1, the same as 0.10.

ep.dec-hundredths.s3.text: Tap to make more gold. 3 rows and 5 more squares make 35 hundredths. That's 0.35.
ep.dec-hundredths.s3.heard: Tap to make more gold. Three rows and five more squares make 35 hundredths. That's 0.35.

ep.dec-hundredths.s4.text: Money works the same way. A dollar is 100 cents, so 35 cents is $0.35.
ep.dec-hundredths.s4.heard: Money works the same way. A dollar is a hundred cents, so 35 cents is 35 hundredths of a dollar.

ep.dec-hundredths.card.text: You won the Hundredths card! Two digits after the point count hundredths, like cents.
ep.dec-hundredths.card.heard: You won the hundredths card. Two numbers after the point count hundredths like cents.

ep.dec-compare.intro.text: Rock Candy Armadillo wants the bigger pile of money. Which is more, 0.5 or 0.45?
ep.dec-compare.intro.heard: Rock Candy Armadillo wants the bigger pile of money. Which is more, 0.5 or 0.45?

ep.dec-compare.s0.text: 0.45 has more digits, so it looks bigger. But is it?
ep.dec-compare.s0.heard: 0.45 has more numbers, so it looks bigger. But is it?

ep.dec-compare.s1.text: Give them the same number of digits. Tap the glowing spot. 0.5 is the same as 0.50.
ep.dec-compare.s1.heard: Give them the same number of digits. Tap the glowing spot. 0.5 is the same as 0.50.

ep.dec-compare.s2.text: In money, 0.50 is 50 cents and 0.45 is 45 cents. Drag the coins onto the plates.
ep.dec-compare.s2.heard: In money, 0.50 is 50 cents and 0.45 is 45 cents. Drag the coins onto the plates.

ep.dec-compare.s3.text: Tap each plate. 50 cents is more than 45 cents, so 0.5 is bigger! Line up the points, fill in a zero, then compare.
ep.dec-compare.s3.heard: Tap each plate. 50 cents is more than 45 cents, so 0.5 is bigger. Line up the points, fill in a zero, then compare.

ep.dec-compare.card.text: You won the Line Up the Points card! Fill in zeros so the digits match, then compare.
ep.dec-compare.card.heard: You won the line up the points card. Fill in zeros so the digits match, then compare.

ep.dec-add.intro.text: Teakettle Dragon sells a muffin for $1.25 and a juice for 50 cents. How much for both?
ep.dec-add.intro.heard: Teakettle Dragon sells a muffin for $1.25 and a juice for $0.50. How much for both?

ep.dec-add.s0.text: The muffin is $1.25. The juice is 50 cents, and we write that $0.50. Line up the points.

ep.dec-add.s2.text: Add the cents first. Tap the glowing spot. 25 and 50 make 75 cents.
ep.dec-add.s2.heard: Add the scents first. Tap the glowing spot. 25 and 50 make 75 cents.

ep.dec-add.s3.text: Then the dollars. 1 dollar and 75 cents is $1.75. The point stays in line!
ep.dec-add.s3.heard: Then the dollars. $1.75 is $1.75. The point stays in line.

ep.dec-add.card.text: You won the Line Up and Add card! Line up the points, then add like whole numbers.
ep.dec-add.card.heard: You won the line up and add card. Line up the points, then add like whole numbers.

ep.frac-parts.intro.text: Sprout Bunny baked a blueberry pie! Let's share it, and learn how to write a fraction.
ep.frac-parts.intro.heard: Sprout bunny baked a blueberry pie. Let's share it and learn how to write a fraction.

ep.frac-parts.s0.text: The pie is cut into 8 equal slices. Equal means every slice is the same size.
ep.frac-parts.s0.heard: The pie is cut into eight equal slices. Equal means every slice is the same size.

ep.frac-parts.s1.text: Bunny wants 3 slices. Drag 3 glowing slices onto the plate!
ep.frac-parts.s1.heard: Bunny wants three slices. Drag three glowing slices onto the plate.

ep.frac-parts.s2.text: The top number is the 3 slices on the plate. The bottom number is all 8 slices. Tap each glowing spot!
ep.frac-parts.s2.heard: The top number is the three slices on the plate. The bottom number is all eight slices. Tap each glowing spot.

ep.frac-parts.card.text: You won the Equal Parts card! The bottom number tells how many equal parts. The top number tells how many you have.
ep.frac-parts.card.heard: You won the Equal Parts card. The bottom number tells how many equal parts. The top number tells how many you have.

ep.frac-one-piece.intro.text: Pebble Tortoise found a chocolate bar in the toy workshop! Let's snap it into pieces.
ep.frac-one-piece.intro.heard: Pebble Tortoise found a chocolate bar in the toy workshop. Let's snap it into pieces.

ep.frac-one-piece.s0.heard: The bar has four equal squares.

ep.frac-one-piece.s1.text: Snap off one square! One of 4 equal pieces is one quarter.
ep.frac-one-piece.s1.heard: Snap off one square. One of four equal pieces is one quarter.

ep.frac-one-piece.s2.text: Snap off two more. Now you have 3 of the 4 pieces. That's three quarters!
ep.frac-one-piece.s2.heard: Snap off two more. Now you have three of the four pieces. That's three quarters.

ep.frac-one-piece.card.text: You won the One Piece card! One of 4 equal pieces is one quarter, and three of them make three quarters.
ep.frac-one-piece.card.heard: You won the one-piece card. One of four equal pieces is one quarter, and three of them make three quarters.

ep.frac-of-a-set.intro.text: Snowdrop Seal packed cupcakes for a picnic! A fraction can be part of a group, too.
ep.frac-of-a-set.intro.heard: Snowdrop seal-packed cupcakes for a picnic. A fraction can be part of a group, too.

ep.frac-of-a-set.s1.text: Snowdrop wants 2 of them. Tap the glowing cupcakes! 2 out of 6 is two sixths.
ep.frac-of-a-set.s1.heard: Snowdrop wants two of them. Tap the glowing cupcakes. Two out of six is two-sixths.

ep.frac-of-a-set.s2.text: Now there are 12 cupcakes and 3 plates. What is one third of 12?
ep.frac-of-a-set.s2.heard: Now there are 12 cupcakes and 3 plates. What is one-third of 12?

ep.frac-of-a-set.s3.text: Share them out! Drag cupcakes onto the plates, and the rest will follow.
ep.frac-of-a-set.s3.heard: Share them out. Drag cupcakes onto the plates, and the rest will follow.

ep.frac-of-a-set.s4.text: One plate is one third. Tap its cupcakes! One third of 12 is 4.
ep.frac-of-a-set.s4.heard: One plate is one-third. Tap its cupcakes. One-third of twelve is four.

ep.frac-of-a-set.card.text: You won the Part of a Set card! 2 of 6 cupcakes is two sixths. One third of 12 means share 12 into 3 groups.
ep.frac-of-a-set.card.heard: You won the part of a set card. Two of six cupcakes is two-sixths. One-third of twelve means share twelve into three groups.

ep.frac-number-line.intro.text: Puddle Pup's plank goes from 0 to 1. Fractions live on the number line too!

ep.frac-number-line.s0.text: The plank from 0 to 1 is cut into 4 equal jumps.

ep.frac-number-line.s1.text: Tap the glowing spot to hop one jump. That's one quarter!
ep.frac-number-line.s1.heard: Tap the glowing spot to hop one jump. That's one quarter.

ep.frac-number-line.s2.text: Hop two more. That's 3 jumps out of 4, or three quarters!
ep.frac-number-line.s2.heard: Hop two more. That's three jumps out of four, or three quarters.

ep.frac-number-line.s3.text: One more hop. Four quarters make one whole!

ep.frac-number-line.card.text: You won the On the Line card! Cut the line from 0 to 1 into equal jumps, then count the jumps.
ep.frac-number-line.card.heard: You win the on-the-line card. Cut the line from 0 to 1 into equal jumps, then count the jumps.

ep.frac-bigger.intro.text: Sprout Bunny has two pies, cut in different ways. Which slice would you pick?
ep.frac-bigger.intro.heard: Sprout bunny has two pies, cut in different ways. Which slice would you pick?

ep.frac-bigger.s0.text: This pie is cut into 3 slices. That one is cut into 8.

ep.frac-bigger.s1.text: Take one slice from each pie. Drag them onto the plates!
ep.frac-bigger.s1.heard: Take one slice from each pie. Drag them onto the plates.

ep.frac-bigger.s2.text: Which is bigger? Tap the glowing spot to find out. Fewer cuts make bigger pieces, so one third is bigger than one eighth!
ep.frac-bigger.s2.heard: Which is bigger? Tap the glowing spot to find out. Fewer cuts make bigger pieces, so one-third is bigger than one-eighth.

ep.frac-bigger.s3.text: When the bottom numbers are the same, more is more. Five eighths is bigger than three eighths.
ep.frac-bigger.s3.heard: When the bottom numbers are the same, more is more. 5 eighths is bigger than 3 eighths.

ep.frac-bigger.card.text: You won the Which Is Bigger card! Same bottom number? More is more. One piece each? Fewer cuts make bigger pieces.
ep.frac-bigger.card.heard: You won the which is bigger card. Same bottom number? More is more. One piece each? Fewer cuts make bigger pieces.

ep.frac-equal.intro.heard: Puddle Pup brought a pizza to the picnic. Can we cut it without changing how much Pup gets?

ep.frac-equal.s0.text: This half is for Pup. That's one half.
ep.frac-equal.s0.heard: This half is for pup. That's one half.

ep.frac-equal.s1.text: Cut every slice in two. Now the pizza has 4 slices.
ep.frac-equal.s1.heard: Cut every slice in two. Now the pizza has four slices.

ep.frac-equal.s2.text: Tap the slices that cover the same as the half. Two quarters!
ep.frac-equal.s2.heard: Tap the slices that cover the same as the half. Two quarters.

ep.frac-equal.s3.text: Cut again. Now there are 8 slices, and 4 of them glow. One half, two quarters and four eighths are all the same amount!
ep.frac-equal.s3.heard: Cut again. Now there are eight slices, and four of them glow. One half, two quarters, and four eighths are all the same amount.

ep.frac-equal.card.heard: You won the same amount card. Same pizza, more cuts. One half is two quarters, and that's four eighths.

ep.frac-add.s2.text: Now two more slices. That's two eighths!
ep.frac-add.s2.heard: Now two more slices. That's 2 eighths.

ep.frac-add.s3.heard: Tap the pink slices to count them all. Three slices, and they're still eighths. That's three eighths. Add the tops, and keep the bottom.

ep.frac-take-away.intro.text: Pebble Tortoise has most of a chocolate bar left, and Pebble's tummy is rumbling!
ep.frac-take-away.intro.heard: Pebble Tortoise has most of a chocolate bar left, and Pebble's tummy is rumbling.

ep.frac-take-away.s0.text: Here are five sixths of a bar.
ep.frac-take-away.s0.heard: Here are five sixths of a bar.

ep.frac-take-away.s1.text: Pebble eats two squares. Tap 2 squares!
ep.frac-take-away.s1.heard: Pebble eats two squares. Tap two squares.

ep.frac-take-away.s2.text: Tap what's left to count it. 3 squares, and they're still sixths. That's three sixths! Take away the tops, and keep the bottom.

ep.frac-mixed.s0.text: Here are 3 empty dishes, and 9 quarter slices. That's nine quarters.
ep.frac-mixed.s0.heard: Here are three empty dishes and nine quarter slices. That's nine quarters.

ep.frac-mixed.s1.text: Fill the dishes! Drag 3 slices, and the rest will follow. 4 quarters make a whole pie.
